title: SDK toolcall contract surface and stream backpressure helpers
creator: Alex Kim
description: Add a cross-language SDK layer that provides: 1) first-class schema validation and coercion helpers for tool/function call contracts; 2) safe invocation helpers that implement progressive retry semantics for partial responses and transient errors; and 3) streaming ergonomics utilities (backpressure-aware async iterators, resumable streams, and explicit cancel semantics). Goal is to reduce customer integration bugs when using tool-calling, improve reliability for partially streamed function responses, and provide shared examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go.
acceptance_criteria: Library exposes a language-idiomatic validateContract(schema, payload) helper that returns typed/coerced payload or a structured validation error
Invocation helper supports: idempotency metadata, retryable vs non-retryable error classification, and progressive retry (fast-fail then backoff) in examples for Python/TS/Go
Streaming helper returns an async iterator (or channel in Go) that supports backpressure via explicit request(n) or buffer-limited reads and a clear cancel() API
Unit tests covering schema coercion edge cases (missing required fields, extra props, type coercion), retry transitions, and stream resume after transient disconnect
Docs and three runnable examples (one per language) demonstrating a tool call that streams a JSON-lines function result and safely resumes after a transient disconnect
technical_notes: Schema format: adopt a constrained subset of OpenAPI/JSON Schema focusing on positional/required arguments and typed primitives to keep coercion deterministic
Coercion rules: string->number parse, number->string stringify, boolean coercion from truthy values, explicit opt-in for lossy casts
Validation API should return a single normalized payload and a diagnostics list (errors with path and suggestion) for developer UX
Retry policy: immediate fast-retry once for transient network hiccups, then exponential backoff with jitter; do NOT retry non-idempotent tool calls unless caller marks request as safe_to_retry
Streaming contract: include 'resume_token' in each stream chunk metadata to permit server-side stateless resume; client stores last-seen token and requests from that token on reconnect
Backpressure semantics: Python/TS use async iterator with optional fetch_size param; Go exposes a buffered channel and RequestMore(n) function to control prefetch
Telemetry: emit token-level counters and retry reason tags to Console for debugging rollout regressions
